To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the antennal movements are generated by a complex system of interactions between the central nervous system, muscles and the antennal joints; (ii) the antennal and the head movements are controlled by a complex system involving the central nervous system; (iii) the antennae and head are controlled by a system that is not symmetrical between the right and the left side of the animal; (iv) there are differences between the control of the head and the antennae; and (v)
the head movement is a result of antennal movement and that the head movement does not affect antennal movement.
(1) there is a strong asymmetry between the right and left antennae in the control of head movement and (2) the antennae are controlled asymmetrically with regard to each other and the head.

the analysis of the antennal movements of two species of millipedes (Polydesmida, Polydesmidae).
the development and application of a new statistical method to describe asymmetries of control in the nervous system.
the development of an approach to the analysis of the control of complex movements.
